name: Le poste des infirmières
camera: close view of the nurses' station at the end of the ward

setting.walls: the same powder-blue walls, a rack of patient charts and a heartbeat monitor on a shelf
setting.landmark: the curved wooden nurses' counter with a pot of sunflowers and a wall board of blank charts
setting.style: S07 gentle storybook painterly 3.5/5 (one style for the whole Quartier de la Santé)

items.scene: A smiling runner jogs past on a shiny curved PROSTHESIS ("proh-TEHZ") blade, giving the nurses a wave.
A cartoon heartbeat line on the monitor bounces back up like a RE-ANIMATED ("ray-ah-nee-mah-SYOHN") cartoon, and the patient teddy wakes up smiling in INTENSIVE CARE.
A nurse explains the knee INFILTRATION ("an-feel-trah-SYOHN"), a gentle injection, to a footballer with an ice pack on his knee, a capped syringe prop in her hand.
A brass wall plaque reads DÉJECTION, DROPPINGS (formal word for excrement); a false friend, not English 'dejection'.
A nurse makes a neat INSERTION ("an-sehr-SYOHN"), slipping a fresh page into a patient's chart.
A toy football has knocked a flowerpot off the counter, and the nurse sighs: PRAY, JUDGE ("pray-zhew-DEES") the HARM done!
A PARAMEDIC in a hi-vis jacket wheels the AMBULANCE ("ahn-bew-lahn-SYAY") stretcher, a smiling teddy aboard, up to the counter.
A beaver at the counter holds up the little twig DAM that burst, water dripping: to his great DISMAY and HARM.

prompt:
Gentle storybook painterly illustration, realism about 3.5/5, soft gouache-and-oil brushwork, warm-hearted and calm, natural NEUTRAL daylight with true colours, off-white whites, no orange, sepia, amber or golden cast, no pink or blue tint, clear readable figures with contact shadows on the floor, consistent eye-level perspective, 16:9 wide composition.
Scene: Le poste des infirmières in the B19_hopital building, second floor (ward). Camera: close view of the nurses' station at the end of the ward.
Setting: the same powder-blue walls, a rack of patient charts and a heartbeat monitor on a shelf; floor: the same pale oak-look floor. Landmark: the curved wooden nurses' counter with a pot of sunflowers and a wall board of blank charts. Light: daylight from the ward windows. The room feels lived-in and real, with depth (never an empty white backdrop).
Paint these exits clearly as walkable openings: the ward floor in the near right foreground (the way back out).
Characters and objects, each a separate, clearly spaced group, feminine-word groups on the left half and masculine-word groups on the right half:
- far left, foreground: A smiling runner jogs past on a shiny curved PROSTHESIS blade, giving the nurses a wave.
- far left, middle distance: INTENSIVE CARE and RESUSCITATION; on the monitor a cartoon ANIMATION of a heartbeat line bounces back up as a patient bear wakes and smiles.
- left, foreground: A nurse explains the knee INJECTION to a footballer, an ice pack on his knee and a capped syringe prop in her hand.
- centre-left, middle distance: a blank brass museum plaque on the wall (no figure).
- centre, foreground: A nurse makes a neat INSERTION, slipping a fresh page into a patient's chart.
- centre-right, middle distance: A toy football has knocked a flowerpot off the counter, and a nurse surveys the HARM done.
- right, foreground: A PARAMEDIC in a hi-vis jacket wheels a stretcher with a smiling teddy up to the counter.
- far right, middle distance: A beaver at the counter holds up the little twig DAM that burst, water dripping: to his great DISMAY and HARM.
Leave a blank light board for the room sign high on the back wall. No written words, letters, numbers or logos anywhere (signs and plaques are blank boards). No blood, no wounds, no needles in skin (syringes only as capped harmless props), no alcohol, no smoking, no religious symbols, no red-cross emblem. Nobody cropped by the image edge; keep every figure well inside the frame with a clear gap between figures. Figures stand on the floor or sit on real furniture, never floating or in rows behind a counter.
